svg.title: Product quantization splits a vector into sub-vectors and stores codebook IDs learned with k-means; it compresses well but needs training. Binary quantization keeps only the sign of each dimension; it needs no training and uses XOR and popcount, so it serves as a rough first pass before an exact rerank.
svg.text: learn codebooks with k-means, per table
good compression, but it needs training,
and codebooks drift as data changes
keep the sign of each dimension
rough, so: first pass, then exact rerank

figure.figcaption: Two ways to shrink a vector. The better compressor lost to the one with no training step.
